clue.text: Worthlessness of tax unknown outside part of UK

indicators.note: the tax word sits outside, wrapping around the part of the UK

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
NI is Northern Ireland
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a tax not known outside one corner of the UK is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the wrapping signal; Y comes from algebra, where x and y stand for unknown quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanity in its older sense is emptiness or futility, things of no real worth.

clue.text: Girl I encountered in Paris, very old capital city

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name
the French for I is je, met by a visitor in Paris

explanation.surface: A tourist recalls a girl met in Paris and a very old capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarajevo is the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

clue.text: Reportedly signed beneath a building

indicators.note: reportedly tells us the phrase for signed beneath is to be heard, not read

parts.note: to sign beneath something is to have written under it

explanation.surface: Gossip says someone put their signature under a building.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'wrote under' (signed beneath) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, typically domed.

clue.text: A whip round welcomed by the diplomatic aide

indicators.note: the word 'the' takes in the turned whip, as a host welcomes a guest
round means the whip word is turned about, read backwards

parts.note: a cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip

explanation.surface: A diplomat's aide passes the hat round and is warmly received.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip round' looks like a collection of money, but splits: 'round' turns the whip into TAC, and 'welcomed by' sets it inside 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a junior official on an ambassador's staff.

clue.text: Literary work some really dislike going over

indicators.note: going over means the run of letters is flipped, read right to left
some means only part of the letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: A literary work that some people dislike intensely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes LLYDI from 'reaLLY DIslike', and 'going over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short poem or prose piece depicting a peaceful rural scene.

clue.text: King escaping, confronted by small number with insidious reach?

indicators.note: by here means the small number stands beside, ahead of, the confronted word

parts.note: ten is a small number

indicators.note: escaping says the king slips out of the word for confronted

parts.note: to tackle is to confront
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king flees, faced by a small band whose influence spreads insidiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping' removes the king and 'by' puts the small number ahead; 'with insidious reach' pictures an octopus-like grip spreading everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature with tentacles can reach out and grasp, so figuratively an influence extending its grip everywhere.

clue.text: Impulsive organist, not one he'd fancy!

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine freely, so the letters are reworked
not says the letter for one is left out of the musician's word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An impetuous organist, not the one he would have liked!
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' drops I from ORGANIST, leaving ORGANST; 'fancy' shuffles that with HED.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstrong person is wilful and rash, acting on impulse.

clue.text: Work round Manx cat?

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the cat word loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a cat

explanation.surface: Some job concerning a cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx cat breed is tailless, so 'Manx' cuts the final S from PUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for a work, especially a musical composition.

clue.text: Welshman crossing Lake Salvador?

indicators.note: the Welshman spans the lake, so its letter sits inside him

parts.note: Dai is a stock Welsh name, short for David

explanation.surface: A Welshman crosses a lake in Salvador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salvador' looks like a place (El Salvador), but it is the first name of the surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador is the first name of the Spanish surrealist painter Dalí.

clue.text: A fine feminine aptitude for good humour

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
aptitude means natural ability

explanation.surface: A fine woman's gift is her good humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Affability is friendliness and good nature, a pleasant easy-going manner.

clue.text: Oddly, Pepys said, it could result from rushing courses

definitions.text: it could result from rushing courses

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The diarist Samuel Pepys remarks on the effect of bolting one's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Pepys was a 17th-century English diarist. 'Courses' are meal courses, not race courses.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is indigestion, which eating meals too fast can bring on.

clue.text: See about the writer's initially being in oblivion

indicators.note: the see word sits about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold
the writer is I, so the writer's (writer is) is I'm

indicators.note: initially takes only the first letter of being

explanation.surface: Someone imagines the author fading into oblivion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer's' is a contraction of 'the writer is', meaning 'I am'; 'about' wraps the see word round that and the B from 'initially being'.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is a state of neglect or being forgotten, cast aside out of mind.

clue.text: Natural disaster way back, touching a friend abroad

indicators.note: back means the way word is read in reverse

parts.note: St is street, a way
un ami is French for a friend

explanation.surface: A natural disaster long ago affected a friend overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ST into TS; 'touching' only joins it to the French UN AMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave, caused by an undersea earthquake.

clue.text: Old club rejected container for wine and wallop

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the container word is reversed

parts.note: a bin is a rack or store for wine bottles
lick is slang for a hard blow

explanation.surface: An old club throws out its wine rack and has a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns BIN into NIB. 'Club' is a golf club, not a society.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old name for a golf iron with a lofted face, about a nine-iron.

clue.text: Bee circling crude sty made without mortar

indicators.note: the bee word goes round, encircling the reworked sty

parts.note: a drone is a male bee

indicators.note: crude means rough, unrefined, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bee flies round a rough pigsty built without mortar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' rearranges the sty into YST, which 'circling' puts inside the bee; a drone is a male honeybee.
explanation.definitionFit: A drystone wall is built of stones fitted together with no cement binding them.

clue.text: What Abraham may have been — critical?

explanation.surface: A wry question about the patriarch's character.
explanation.walkthrough: Abraham came from Ur of the Chaldees, so he was a gentleman of Ur: a 'Ur gent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham, from the city of Ur, was perhaps a gentleman thence; critical means pressing or demanding attention.

clue.text: Put coat on and disappeared across river

indicators.note: across means the disappearing word stretches over, so the river is inside it

parts.note: vanished means disappeared

explanation.surface: Someone put on a coat and vanished over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put coat on' reads as dressing to leave, but it is a coat of paint or lacquer.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnished means given a glossy protective layer, a coat applied to wood.

clue.text: Dapper knight on board, always carrying Times …

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: carrying means the always word holds the times letters within it

parts.note: ay is an old word for always
T is times, so TT for the plural

explanation.surface: A smart knight on board, forever carrying the Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts the times inside the old word for always. 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but T is the multiplication sign read aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neat and smart in dress, stylishly turned out.

clue.text: Lust seen, curiously, as discordant?

indicators.note: curiously means strangely, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Is lust, viewed oddly, out of harmony?
explanation.definitionFit: Tuneless means lacking melody, so harsh or out of key.

clue.text: A couple of advantages — on many occasions

explanation.surface: Two benefits, recurring frequently.
explanation.walkthrough: Two advantages are 'a gain and a gain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gain is a benefit, so two of them make a pair of them; the phrase also means repeatedly.

clue.text: Erring husband leaves receptacle for remains

indicators.note: leaves means the husband departs, so his letter is taken out

parts.note: an ashtray holds the remains of cigarettes

explanation.surface: An unfaithful husband walks out, leaving behind an urn of ashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' suggests a funeral urn; they are cigarette ash and stubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Astray means off the right path, wandering into wrongdoing.

clue.text: Cute play unexpectedly supported by current oil producers

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece supported sits above, so the current letter comes beneath
unexpectedly means in surprising fashion, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A charming show unexpectedly backed by oil companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges CUTEPLAY into EUCALYPT, and I goes underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalyptus trees yield eucalyptus oil from their leaves.

clue.text: Fell for this nymph's domain?

parts.note: fell is a mountain, so the clue asks for the nymph whose home is the mountains, not someone who fell for her

explanation.surface: Someone fell for a nymph, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' reads as a verb (fell in love), but is a noun: a hill or mountain, as in the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the oreads were nymphs of mountains and hills.

clue.text: Seeking a trendy style, to some extent

parts.note: to be after something is to seek it
a fashion is a trendy style

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a modish look, up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something after a fashion is doing it partly or not very well.

clue.text: Drinks said to engross a breed of duck?

indicators.note: said means the drinks word is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: ales are drinks
to bury oneself in something is to be engrossed by it

explanation.surface: Drinks, it is said, absorb a kind of duck.
explanation.walkthrough: AYLES sounds like 'ales' (drinks); BURY, as in burying oneself in work, is to engross.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aylesbury is a white domestic duck bred in Buckinghamshire, England.

clue.text: Access to power Kentucky Republican enlisted to rise rapidly

indicators.note: enlisted means taken into the ranks, so these letters go inside the power word

parts.note: a socket gives access to electric power
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: A Kentucky Republican is recruited to gain power fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Access to power' suggests political office; it is an electric socket.
explanation.definitionFit: To skyrocket is to soar or increase very fast, like a firework.

clue.text: Amount of pressure girl talked of at pub?

indicators.note: talked of means the girl's name is spoken, giving letters spelt differently

parts.note: Milly is a girl's name
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Pressure is put on a girl discussed at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A millibar is a unit of air pressure, one thousandth of a bar.

clue.text: Quibbler quietly meets poet, putting final point first

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: the final letter, E, is a compass point that moves to the front of the poet

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet

explanation.surface: A nitpicker quietly meets a poet and puts his last point first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting final point first' moves the end E of DANTE to the start, giving EDANT; E is a compass point (east).
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant fusses over trivial details and rules, splitting hairs.

clue.text: Unstylish, but invited out regularly?

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned, yet often asked out?
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is someone often asked out romantically.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated means old-fashioned; someone regularly taken out on romantic outings has been courted.

clue.text: Person who's graduated in Eastern state

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate living in an eastern US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a state in the north-eastern United States.
